subject.title: Feature Request: config:pre-apply hook for validating config changes

question: Should OpenClaw add a synchronous plugin/API-level config pre-apply veto, and if so what trust, ordering, and failure semantics should it guarantee?
rationale: The missing behavior is real, but the permanent API shape affects plugin contracts, secrets/config security boundaries, gateway availability, and upgrade behavior, so automation should not choose it unilaterally.

options.title: Design the hook in the RFC
options.body: Keep this issue open and define the config pre-apply hook contract, ordering, rejection result, actor metadata, and tests as part of the config validation/mutation RFC.

options.title: Fold into broader preflight only
options.body: Track this as a narrower part of the broader preflight framework and do not add a separate write-time plugin veto until that framework owns config mutation policy.

options.title: Reject plugin veto for now
options.body: Close this direction and rely on built-in validation plus guarded agent tools, accepting that external validators cannot forcibly intercept all config writes.

recommendation.title: Design the hook in the RFC
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and define the config pre-apply hook contract, ordering, rejection result, actor metadata, and tests as part of the config validation/mutation RFC.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the clearest current discussion owner from the issue thread and already framed the API gap against the RFC direction.
